body:
## Distance Fades in Many Dimensions

In a room with thousands of directions, the nearest and farthest points can become surprisingly similar in distance. Neighborhoods stop feeling local.

This is part of the curse of dimensionality. Feature selection, compression, or a distance shaped by domain knowledge can restore useful neighborhoods.

SVM boundaries depend only on support vectors because other points sit safely away from the margin. Dual optimization makes kernels possible by working through pairwise similarities.
common_mistakes: Using either method before scaling features.
Choosing K or kernel settings on the test set.
Assuming KNN training is costly while ignoring its prediction-time search.

real_world_usage: These contrasting methods teach how distance, boundaries, and scaling shape classification.
